content.5.3.3 Other laboratory biomarkers: Lactate indicates tissue oxygen supply/demand imbalance and elevated arterial plasma lactate (>2 mmol/L) predicts PE-related complications. Elevated serum creatinine and reduced (calculated) glomerular filtration rate are related to 30-day all-cause mortality in acute PE. Neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and cystatin C, both markers of acute kidney injury, are of prognostic value. Hyponatraemia predicts in-hospital mortality in acute PE (meta-analysis). Vasopressin is released with stress/hypotension/low cardiac output; its surrogate marker copeptin has been reported useful for risk stratification in acute PE, with specific copeptin cut-offs associated with increased risk. Results were confirmed in multiple cohorts.
content.5.4 Combined parameters and scores for a: Individual baseline findings may not suffice to classify PE severity; combinations of clinical, imaging, and laboratory parameters are used to build prognostic scores (e.g., Bova score). H-FABP (heart-type fatty acid binding protein) and high-sensitivity troponin T have been validated in cohort studies and are used in risk scores (Syncope, Tachycardia/FAST). A combination of RV dysfunction on echocardiogram or CTPA together with a positive cardiac troponin test has been directly tested as a guide for early therapeutic decisions in a large RCT of PE patients without haemodynamic instability.
